patient_can_communicate_sufficiently_now.assessment: The patient is able to speak fluently, though with errors such as word substitutions, and frequently interrupts the examiner, indicating the ability to communicate at least verbally.
patient_can_communicate_sufficiently_now.evidence: His speech was fluent, but he often used similar-sounding word substitutions. He frequently interrupted the examiner.

patient_can_hear_sufficiently_now.assessment: The patient engaged with the examiner, attempted to follow commands, and responded to instructions, which suggests adequate hearing ability.
patient_can_hear_sufficiently_now.evidence: He could not follow commands involving multiple steps and was unable to perform simple calculations.

patient_can_see_sufficiently_now.assessment: Patient repeatedly reached for objects and the examiner's tie and face, showing he can perceive and respond to visual stimuli.
patient_can_see_sufficiently_now.evidence: He repeatedly reached out to grab things in front of him, including the examiner's tie and face.

patient_can_undergo_neuropsychological_t.assessment: Patient was able to participate in bedside cognitive assessment (spelling 'world', recall, calculations), so can participate in cognitive testing.
patient_can_undergo_neuropsychological_t.evidence: He could not spell the word 'world' backward, could not follow commands involving multiple steps and was unable to perform simple calculations.

patient_has_finding_of_basic_activity_of.assessment: Patient lives with wife and son (as they brought him), and requires help with dressing, bathing, toileting, and walking, so daily living activity is part of his home context.
patient_has_finding_of_basic_activity_of.evidence: He is unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently. An 89-year-old man was brought to the emergency department by his wife and son.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_frontotemporal_.assessment: Six-month progression of behavioral change, disinhibition, language disturbance, and executive dysfunction fit clinical frontotemporal dementia syndrome.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_frontotemporal_.evidence: Six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality... poor memory, difficulty expressing himself, and unusual behaviors, such as pouring milk onto the table and undressing immediately after getting dressed.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_pick_complex_no.assessment: Chart does not specify Pick's disease or Pick complex diagnosis; only frontotemporal dementia syndrome is described.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_primary_progres.assessment: Patient has fluent speech with word substitute errors, but the main syndrome is behavioral/executive; chart does not specify primary progressive aphasia diagnosis.

patient_has_undergone_computerized_axial.assessment: There is no mention of a recent CT scan having been performed.
No evidence in the vignette of any CT scan, much less one showing anterior lobar degeneration.

patient_has_undergone_magnetic_resonance.assessment: The chart is silent regarding whether a recent MRI was performed, so we defer to the in-person visit as per doctrine on inclusion atom silence.
No MRI findings are described; chart is silent on the presence of frontotemporal lobar atrophy. Doctrine dictates permissive null for inclusion-side silence.

patient_assessment_using_mini_mental_sta.assessment: The chart does not specify a MMSE score or any related number; performance on cognitive tasks is described but not formally quantified. Default to null on inclusion-side silence.

__THRESH__::patient_assessment_using_min.assessment: There is no explicit MMSE score; chart describes severe cognitive impairment but does not state whether MMSE > 5. Doctrine for inclusion-side threshold atom: permissive null.

patient_number_of_basic_activities_of_da.assessment: Chart states the patient is 'unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently,' which strongly suggests that he lacks the opportunity to perform these basic ADLs.
patient_number_of_basic_activities_of_da.evidence: He is unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently.

__THRESH__::patient_number_of_basic_acti.assessment: Patient is described as unable to perform any basic activities of daily living independently, so threshold of at least 1 is not met.
__THRESH__::patient_number_of_basic_acti.evidence: He is unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently.

patient_has_finding_of_abnormal_liver_fu.assessment: There is no mention of liver disease, abnormal liver labs, or clinical signs referable to abnormal liver function in the vignette.

patient_has_finding_of_amnestic_disorder.assessment: The patient displays poor memory with immediate recall preserved and severe impairment at 5 minutes (0/3 words), indicating a significant amnestic syndrome.
patient_has_finding_of_amnestic_disorder.evidence: "He could immediately recall three out of three words but recalled none of them after 5 minutes."

patient_has_finding_of_amnestic_disorder.assessment: The case describes prominent language disturbance, personality change, behavioral disinhibition, and paratonia—classically frontotemporal dementia—not the predominantly amnestic syndrome typical of Alzheimer's; memory loss is present but with marked frontal features.
patient_has_finding_of_amnestic_disorder.evidence: "difficulty expressing himself"; "exhibited unusual behaviors"; "speech was fluent, but he often used similar-sounding word substitutions"; "paratonic rigidity"

patient_has_finding_of_amnestic_disorder.assessment: The charted clinical picture is most compatible with frontotemporal dementia/Pick complex, as described by behavioral disinhibition, language disturbance, and executive dysfunction.
patient_has_finding_of_amnestic_disorder.evidence: "progressive changes in cognition and personality"; "difficulty expressing himself"; "unusual behaviors"; "paratonic rigidity"

patient_has_finding_of_disorder_of_cardi.assessment: The heart rate is irregular, suggesting possible atrial fibrillation, but there is no indication of clinical instability or overt cardiovascular disease (e.g., heart failure, angina, recent MI). 'Clinically significant' is not established.
patient_has_finding_of_disorder_of_cardi.evidence: "the heart rate 61 bpm in an irregular rhythm"

patient_has_finding_of_disorder_of_cardi.assessment: No evidence of a clinically significant cardiovascular disorder: irregular rhythm is noted, but no sequelae, symptoms, or instability are described.
patient_has_finding_of_disorder_of_cardi.evidence: "the heart rate 61 bpm in an irregular rhythm"

patient_has_diagnosis_of_degenerative_br.assessment: The patient meets clinical criteria for a neurodegenerative disorder due to progressive dementia with behavioral and language features and neurological findings.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_degenerative_br.evidence: "six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality"; "paratonic rigidity"; "myoclonic jerks"

patient_has_diagnosis_of_degenerative_br.assessment: Symptoms align with frontotemporal dementia/Pick complex; there is no evidence of another (non-FTD/PC) neurodegenerative disorder.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_degenerative_br.evidence: "progressive changes in cognition and personality" with "difficulty expressing himself" and "unusual behaviors"

patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_now.assessment: The patient exhibits progressive changes in cognition and personality, memory loss, inability to perform activities of daily living, and severe impairments in executive function—all signs consistent with current dementia.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_now.evidence: Six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality; poor memory; unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently; could not follow commands; unable to perform calculations.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_now@@o.assessment: The chart does not provide an explicit diagnosis or specify etiology for dementia; no mention of acute cerebral injury, cerebrovascular disease, hypoxic damage, vitamin deficiencies, infection, or neoplasia, nor Alzheimer's disease. Etiology remains unspecified in chart.

patient_has_finding_of_allergy_to_drug_i.assessment: No mention of history of drug allergy; in PRESCREEN doctrine, silence implies no history.
No mention of severe drug allergy; under prescreen doctrine, chart silence is evidence against history.

patient_has_finding_of_endocrine_disease.assessment: No mention of any endocrine disease; chart silence defaults to no active endocrine disorder.
No evidence of clinically significant endocrine disease is provided; silence implies absence.

patient_has_finding_of_hypersensitivity_.assessment: No mention of hypersensitivity to bromide; silence defaults to no history.
No mention of hypersensitivity to choline agonists; silence defaults to no history.
No mention of hypersensitivity to cholinesterase inhibitors; silence defaults to no history.
No mention of hypersensitivity to similar agents; silence defaults to no history.

patient_has_finding_of_impaired_cognitio.assessment: The chart documents progressive changes in cognition, poor memory, impaired calculation, inability to follow commands, and abnormal behaviors consistent with ongoing cognitive impairment.
patient_has_finding_of_impaired_cognitio.evidence: six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality...poor memory, difficulty expressing himself...unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently...could not follow commands involving multiple steps and was unable to perform simple calculations

patient_has_finding_of_impaired_cognitio.assessment: No mention of acute cerebral injury as contributing to current cognitive impairment; chart describes insidious, progressive course consistent with neurodegeneration.
No mention of cerebral neoplasia (brain tumor) as the cause; progressive symptoms and exam findings suggest neurodegeneration, not neoplasm.
No mention of stroke, vascular disease, or stepwise decline; the course is gradual and progressive, not suggestive of cerebrovascular etiology.
No history or findings suggestive of hypoxic brain injury as etiology (e.g., cardiac arrest, anoxic event) noted.
No history suggesting CNS infection (e.g., fever, rapidly progressive confusion) is present.
No evidence of vitamin deficiency states or related reversible causes are described.

patient_has_finding_of_impairment_of_reg.assessment: Patient is unable to recall any of three words after five minutes, indicating a disturbance of memory registration.
patient_has_finding_of_impairment_of_reg.evidence: He could immediately recall three out of three words but recalled none of them after 5 minutes.

patient_has_finding_of_impairment_of_reg.assessment: Memory impairment is in the setting of documented progressive changes in cognition and behavior, consistent with a clinical picture of frontotemporal dementia or Pick complex; no evidence suggests an alternative etiology.
patient_has_finding_of_impairment_of_reg.evidence: six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality

patient_has_finding_of_kidney_disease_no.assessment: There is no mention of kidney disease or symptoms suggestive of renal dysfunction in the chart, so by exclusion-side prescreen doctrine we default to FALSE.
patient_has_finding_of_kidney_disease_no.evidence: silent: no reference to kidney disease or kidney-related symptoms

patient_has_finding_of_disorder_of_lung_.assessment: The patient had normal respiratory rate and the chart does not mention lung disease or respiratory symptoms; per exclusion-side default, set to FALSE.
patient_has_finding_of_disorder_of_lung_.evidence: silent: no reference to lung disorder, normal respiratory rate

patient_has_finding_of_mental_disorder_n.assessment: While the patient has dementia with behavioral symptoms, these are neurologic manifestations of his primary neurodegenerative disorder (the inclusion disease); there is no mention of a distinct, clinically significant psychiatric disease like schizophrenia, depression, or mania.
patient_has_finding_of_mental_disorder_n.evidence: silent: no reference to separate mental/psychiatric disorder outside dementia

patient_has_finding_of_metabolic_disease.assessment: The chart gives no indication of metabolic disease (e.g., diabetes, thyroid, electrolyte disorders) nor symptoms thereof; per exclusion-side doctrine, default to FALSE.
patient_has_finding_of_metabolic_disease.evidence: silent: no mention of metabolic disease

patient_has_finding_of_peptic_ulcer_now.assessment: There is no information about gastrointestinal complaints, diagnoses, or treatment for ulcers; silent on this exclusion, so FALSE per exclusion-side default.
patient_has_finding_of_peptic_ulcer_now.evidence: silent: no mention of peptic ulcer or GI symptoms

patient_has_finding_of_epilepsy_control_.assessment: The chart describes myoclonic jerks in the arms but does not document a diagnosis of epilepsy or active seizure events, nor mention any anticonvulsant therapy or history of seizures; myoclonus can be present in neurodegenerative disorders, separate from epilepsy.
patient_has_finding_of_epilepsy_control_.evidence: Myoclonic jerks were seen in the arms... (no mention of epilepsy or seizures, chart silent on epilepsy diagnosis and management)

patient_has_finding_of_urinary_outflow_o.assessment: There is no mention of urinary symptoms, retention, catheterization, or outflow obstruction in the provided chart.
patient_has_finding_of_urinary_outflow_o.evidence: silent: defer to restrictive default (no exclusion fires on silence)

patient_has_finding_of_on_anti_dementia_.evidence: silent: defer to restrictive default (no exclusion fires on silence)
